header.title: P.Oxy. 88 5655: Formulary for exorcism against demons causing illness: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Greek magical papyri and amulets
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:dclp:976535:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY 4.0: credit papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (the source's own licence is CC BY 3.0) and this AI translation.

notes.1.2: Many letters are dotted as doubtful in the edition. Line 2 keeps only the ending -ousa, and line 15 only scraps of two words. “Encounter” (συνάντημα) is the term for a demonic attack. The divine name YHWH is written in Paleo-Hebrew letters in lines 8 and 16 (in 16 the yod is restored); “sent by YHWH” could also be read “sent under YHWH”. *aponōdōsis* is an unidentified word, perhaps corrupt. In line 11 the editor deletes a superfluous “or”.

nodes.text: [...] all things, I adjure, by the name of the L[ord]
which is also called a demon and which comes upon
a soul, of whatever sort it may be, and of what sort, and whatever ki[nd],
whether male or female, sent by YHWH
to do harm to a soul and to kill [it];
every encounter of epilepsy or madness or
derangement of mind, or [by] a deaf encounter
or a voiceless one, or of *aponōdōsis*, or of insensibility,
or [an encount]er of convulsion or gnashing or foaming,
[or an encount]er of miscarriage or of folly
